The study "Evaluating the Use and Acceptance of eLearning for Tertiary Education among Senior High School Students" by Patricia O. Calora and Yrelle Mae R. Lleva examines eLearning and Open and Distance eLearning (ODeL) as solutions to resource challenges in Philippine higher education. Using a quantitative design grounded in the Unified Theory of Acceptance and Use of Technology 2 (UTAUT2), researchers surveyed 200 senior high school students across five K-12 strands to assess their perceptions and intentions regarding online undergraduate studies.

Findings indicate that 71.2% of respondents intend to enroll in an online institution. Most participants were 17-year-old females who use smartphones to access the internet. While students perceive eLearning as flexible and affordable, they lack specific knowledge regarding the practical mechanics of online assessments and virtual collaboration.

Analysis of UTAUT constructs showed that performance expectancy was the only significant predictor of behavioral intention; students more likely to pursue online education were those who believed eLearning would help them achieve academic goals. Other factors, such as effort expectancy, social influence, facilitating conditions, hedonic motivation, price value, and habit, were not significant predictors. The authors conclude that intention is driven by perceived utility for academic success. They recommend that institutions implement communication campaigns to explain online system functions and suggest that developers prioritize resource accessibility, student support, and interactive environments.

The article "Exploring the Potential of a Ticketing-Based Student Support System for Open and Distance e-Learning Institutions" investigates how automated ticketing systems can enhance quality assurance in student support services within Open and Distance e-Learning (ODeL) environments. Because face-to-face interaction is limited in ODeL settings, reliable and timely support is vital for student retention and success.

At the University of the Philippines Open University (UPOU) within the Bachelor of Arts in Multimedia Studies (BAMS) program, students previously relied on at least eight different formal and informal online sources for information. This fragmentation leads to confusion and the risk of following outdated information. Institutional challenges identified include inconsistent response times, difficulties in record-keeping, loss of information during staff turnover, and the difficulty of providing personalized support to a diverse online student body.

Using a qualitative methodology, the researchers conducted a literature review and performed stakeholder interviews with BAMS students, alumni, and support staff. Findings indicate that ticketing-based systems offer significant benefits, such as improved workflows through automation, 24/7 access to a knowledge base, and data analytics insights. The implementation of Freshdesk in the BAMS program showed positive results by providing a centralized knowledge base that allows students to find solutions via articles before filing a ticket. This ensures information is accurate and up-to-date, while the ticketing feature ensures queries are tracked until resolution.

The authors conclude that ticketing-based systems are a promising intervention to improve support quality by making processes more efficient and responsive. They recommend that ODeL institutions adopt such systems as part of quality assurance frameworks, prioritizing ease of use and staff training. Institutions should also inform students of correct support channels to prevent the use of informal ones.

The article "Automated Student Advising: An App for Greater Efficiency" examines logistical challenges in academic advising within the Faculty of Information and Communication Studies (FICS) at the University of the Philippines Open University (UPOU). In an open and distance e-learning environment, the transition to a one-time enrollment model rendered manual practices, such as face-to-face meetings for nominating advisers, insufficient. The lack of an automated system caused difficulties in record-keeping, managing faculty workloads, and reducing human error during committee designation for the DComm, MDC, and BAMS programs.

To resolve these issues, researchers developed the Online Advisory Committee (AdCom) App using an Iterative Incremental Model. The system features three user categories: Students, Advisers, and Administrators. Students can select committee members based on faculty names, photos, and research specializations, while a "quota" filter ensures equitable faculty workloads. Once a nomination is submitted, the system sends automated emails to faculty for acceptance or declination. Administrators can manage profiles, adjust quotas, and generate the official Nomination and Designation of Dissertation Committee Form.

Findings indicate that the AdCom App successfully enables students to formulate committees online. By displaying research interests, the app helps students make informed decisions to ensure committee members complement their research topics. The system streamlines administrative tasks through automated form generation and provides an efficient method for managing faculty loads. The researchers conclude that the app offers a more convenient, sustainable, and paperless method of student support compared to manual practices.

The study "Towards an Age-friendly University: An Intergenerational Study among FICS-UPOU Graduates" examines the educational experiences of graduates from the Faculty of Information and Communication Studies at the University of the Philippines Open University for the 2017-2018 academic year. Aligned with the Age-Friendly University Global Network, the research investigates whether the university's instructional design and curriculum facilitate inclusive, intergenerational learning within an open and distance e-Learning context.

The methodology involved surveying graduates from five FICS programs, categorized into Baby Boomers, Generation X, and Millennials. The assessment evaluated curriculum relevance, program usefulness, quality of instruction, effectiveness of online delivery, and current employability. Findings indicated that the majority of respondents were Millennials, followed by Generation X and Baby Boomers. Overall, respondents reported a highly positive learning experience, with the highest mean score attributed to program usefulness and the lowest to the effectiveness of online delivery.

Statistical analysis revealed that gender and age group were not significantly associated with the learning experience, suggesting the curriculum is age-friendly across generations. However, employment status showed a significant, weak inverse correlation with both the effectiveness of online delivery and current employability, indicating that full-time employment may present challenges. The study concludes that while UPOU provides an inclusive curriculum, instructional design could be refined to better support working professionals.
